import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
coffee_sales = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Convert date column to datetime
coffee_sales['date'] = pd.to_datetime(coffee_sales['date'])

# Melt the data to prepare for bar chart
coffee_sales_melted = pd.melt(coffee_sales, id_vars=['date', 'time', 'product', 'size', 'price', 'quantity', 'payment_method', 'customer_age_group', 'is_takeaway', 'total'],
                              value_vars=['quantity', 'price', 'total'],
                              var_name='category',
                              value_name='value')

# Group by category and customer age group, then calculate mean value
coffee_sales_grouped = coffee_sales_melted.groupby(['category', 'customer_age_group'])['value'].mean().reset_index()

# Pivot the data to prepare for bar chart
coffee_sales_pivoted = coffee_sales_grouped.pivot(index='customer_age_group', columns='category', values='value')

# Plot the data using seaborn
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.barplot(data=coffee_sales_pivoted, palette='viridis')
plt.title('Average Quantity, Price, and Total by Customer Age Group')
plt.xlabel('Customer Age Group')
plt.ylabel('Average Value')
plt.legend(title='Category')
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
